sections.text_helper: Section 73.6 "OTG as a USB peripheral" in chapter 73 (USB on-the-go high-speed (OTG)), RM0486 Rev 4, page 3765.
sections.section_content:
This section gives the functional description of the OTG in the USB peripheral mode. The
OTG works as an USB peripheral in the following circumstances:
• OTG B-Peripheral
– OTG B-device default state if B-side of USB cable is plugged in
• B-device
– If the ID line is present, functional and connected to the B-side of the USB cable.
• Peripheral only
– The force device mode bit (FDMOD) in the Section73.14.4: OTG USB
configuration register (OTG_GUSBCFG) is set to 1, forcing the OTG core to work
as an USB peripheral-only. In this case, the ID line is ignored even if it is present
on the USB connector.
Note: To build a bus-powered device implementation in case of the B-device or peripheral-only
configuration, an external regulator has to be added, that generates the necessary power-
supply from VBUS.
1. Use a regulator to build a bus-powered device.
